replacements.originalStem: A smooth horizontal pipe narrows from section X to section Y, and water flows steadily. Relative to X, Y has:
originalOptionTexts: Lower speed and higher static pressure
Higher speed and higher static pressure
Unchanged speed and unchanged static pressure
Higher speed and lower static pressure
replacements.proposedStem: In a horizontal, unbranched pipe, water flows steadily and incompressibly from a wider section X to a narrower section Y. Assume negligible viscous losses, no pumps or turbines, and compare points on the same streamline. Relative to X, Y has:

proposedOptions.text: Lower speed and higher static pressure
Higher speed and higher static pressure
Unchanged speed and unchanged static pressure
Higher speed and lower static pressure

replacements.explanation: Conservation of volume discharge gives AX vX = AY vY. Because AY is smaller, vY is larger. Along the same horizontal ideal streamline without head loss or shaft work, PX + (ρvX²)/2 = PY + (ρvY²)/2, so PY - PX = (ρ/2)(vX² - vY²) < 0. Thus section Y has higher speed and lower static pressure (D).

replacements.originalStem: A water stream rises in a tube of unchanged area. Which pair of energy terms is unchanged and increased, respectively?
originalOptionTexts: Pressure term increased; gravitational term decreased
Kinetic term decreased; gravitational term decreased
Kinetic term unchanged; gravitational term increased
Kinetic term increased; gravitational term unchanged
replacements.proposedStem: Water flows steadily and incompressibly without leaks through an unbranched tube of constant cross-sectional area, rising from a lower section to a higher one. Which pair of energy terms is unchanged and increased, respectively?

proposedOptions.text: Pressure term increased; gravitational term decreased
Kinetic term decreased; gravitational term decreased
Kinetic term unchanged; gravitational term increased
Kinetic term increased; gravitational term unchanged

replacements.explanation: For an unbranched, leak-free, steady incompressible stream, the discharge Q = Av is constant. Since A is the same at both stations, v is the same, so ½ρv² is unchanged. The higher point has greater ρgh, so the gravitational energy term increases. The source correct answer remains C. This alone does not guarantee individual FBISE B40 Application certification.

replacements.originalStem: A fluid moves steadily in a horizontal pipe with the same cross-sectional area at both points. Ignoring losses and pumps, its static pressures are:
replacements.proposedStem: An incompressible fluid flows steadily through an unbranched horizontal pipe of equal cross-sectional area at points X and Y. Assume both points lie on the same streamline, with negligible viscous losses and no pumps or turbines between them. The static pressures at X and Y are:
replacements.explanation: For steady incompressible no-leak flow, Q = Av is constant. Equal AX and AY give vX = vY. Because both points are horizontal and the same ideal lossless streamline is used, PX + ½ρvX² = PY + ½ρvY²; hence PX = PY (C). Compressible flow can have different densities and speeds at equal area, so the original unqualified premise was under-specified.
